answers.answerContent: အနတ္တလက္ခဏသုတ် and ဓမ္မစကြာပွင့်တော်မူသုတ် were taught at similar times in the park.
At the မိဂဒါဝုန်တော, ကောဏ္ဍည, ဝပ္ပ, ဘဒ္ဒိယ, မဟာနာမ, အဿဇ္ဇိ were all preached.
I am familiar with ဘုရားဆုပန်အကြောင်း but I think I don't specifically remember much.
တပုဿနှင့် and ဘလ္လိက were the first to become followers and arahants of the Buddha
I remember that the Buddha-to-be at that time achieved many interesting feats in childhood like the levitation that he was able to do as a small child, as seen in the picture.
The first people to take refuge in the 2 jewels were the merchants after donating food and water days after the Buddha's enlightenment.
These were a group of followers that were highly enlightened and because of that, get the title of arahants.
The Buddha sent out all the disciples to spread the Dhamma independently because he wanted best for the welfare of the world.

I remember that in order to become a Buddha countless century and eons must be devoted to becoming so. It is also imperative to not practice meditation in such extremes or mildness, and after succeeding and winning over Mara's army, the Buddha-to-be was able to become a Buddha.
I can remember that I believe that is the Buddha, I've done the other lessons of the Buddha, and more.
When the first 5 were taught, the sangha was started.
The Buddha started being able to see what is good, or wholesome, and what is not. He was able to understand more about why different results happen in life.
He realized that he had become obsessed with worldly things such as wealth, and things that only remain during one life.
Things including the triple jewels, truly seeing good from bad, and full enlightenment, like seen in the Buddha would not exist.
To improve the welfare of the world in general, to keep finding peace through the Dhamma, and more.

I think I remember that the Buddha-to-be wanted to achieve more than worldly things such as wealth and more, after seeing the suffering that was inevitable, after riding in the carriage around the kingdom.
